dedupe_keys.name: combining expert and crowd sourced training data to map urban form and functions for the continental us

description: Combining expert and crowd-sourced training data to map urban form and functions for the continental US is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Matthias Demuzere et al. Although continental urban areas are relatively small, they are major drivers of environmental change at local, regional and global scales. Moreover, they are especially vulnerable to these changes owing to the concentration of population and their exposure to a range of hydro-meteorological hazards. Spatially detailed information is used to assess these hazards in urbanized areas. Coverage: global; published in 2020. Formats: Shapefile. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 4874 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
